FOREWORD This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards on 19 June 1989, after the draft finalized by the Shipbuilding Sectional Committee had been approved by the Transport Engineering Division Council. The positioning of ships' round windows on ships intended for international voyage assumes greater The safe position of the round windows is depenimportance for their safe and efficient functioning. dent on their strength relative to external forces acting upon the ship. Therefore, there is a need for adopting a standard practice for calculating the design pressures to be observed when positioning the round windows. The formulae for calculation of design pressure is given in Annex A. The graphs for positioning of round windows given in Annex B are based on the calculation method for design pressures given in Annex A, but are presented in a simplified form for the positioning of round windows. In the preparation of this standard, assistance has been derived from IS0 5780 : 1987' Shipbuilding Side scuttles - Positioning', issued by the International Organization for Standardization ( IS0 ) which takes into account the requirements of International Convention on Load Lines, 1966 ( LL - 1966 ) of International Maritime Organization ( IMO ) and Requirement S3 - Strength of End Bulkheads of Superstructure and Deckhouses, of International Association of Classification Societies ( IACS ).

IS 12693 :1989

Indian Standard POSITIONING OF SHIPS' ROUND WINDOWS - (XJIDELINES
1 SCOPE 1.1This standard specifies the allowable positionwindows applicable for ing of ships' round passenger and cargo ships intended for international voyages. 2 CONDITIONS 2.1 General The positioning of round windows shall be determined according to the rules and regulations of and codes, national international conventions authorities and classification societies. 2.2 Positioning The position depends on: of a round window on a ship FOR POSITIONItiG 2.3.2 If the vessel is required to satisfy damage stability requirements, all round windows whose sills are positioned below the final waterline in damaged conditions and are fitted outside the spaces considered flooded, shall be of the nonopening type. 2.3.3 NO round-window shall be fitted between the position as defined in 2.3.1 and 2.3.2 and the lower part of the curve derived from graph No. 1 ( see Annex B ).
NOTE -Breadth B in relation to a ship means the maximum breadth of the ship measured amid ships to the moulded line of the frame in the case of a ship having a metal shell, or to the outer surface of the hull in the case of a ship having a hull of other material.

2.4 Deadlights 2.4.1 In ships' sides or in the first tier of superstructure or in deckhouses which give access to spaces below the freeboard deck, only round windows with permanently attached deadlight shall be fitted. 2.4.2 Spaces in the second tier which give direct access to closed first-tier superstructures or to spaces below the freeboard deck shall be fitted with round windows with permanently attached deadlights.
NOTE - For detailed information, see Regulation 2.3 ( I ) of LL-1966 with relevant interpretations adopted by the Maritime Safety Committee of IMO.

4 the position of the round window relative

to the length L of the ship and to the height, v, of its sill* above the summer load line, S ( see Graph No. 1 to 4 in Annex B ). Where timber load lines are assigned, the height shall be measured from the summer timber load line to the sill of the round window. in which it is fitted, namely,

2) the fronts, sides and aft ends of superstructures and deckhouses. 2.3 Round Window Position Limitations For positions where round windows shall not be installed, see 2.3.1 and 2.3.3 and where they shall be of non-opening type, see 2.3.2. 2.3.1 No round window shall be installed in a position where its sill would be below a line drawn parallel to the freeboard deck on the side having its lowest point 2.5 percent of the breadth, B, of the ship above the summer load line, S ( or summer timber load line, if assigned ), or 500 mm above the same load line whichever is the greater distance. __-._-*Sill opening. is defined as the lower end of the glass

3 STRENGTH LIMITATIONS 3.1 In addition to the limitations on the use of round windows stipulated in 2.3 the lowest permissible position of round windows is dependent on their strength relative to the external forces acting upon the ship. 3.2 Calculation of External Forces The expected maximum external forces ( design pressure ) are found by the calculation method given in Annex A. 3.3 Ultimate Position No round window shall be installed in any part of the ship where the design pressure exceeds the maximum allowable pressure which individual types and sizes of round windows can withstand, as given in Table 1. 1

CALCULATION OF DESIGN PRESSURE A-l INTRODUCTION A-l.1 The design pressure to be observed when positioning ships' round windows is determined according to the formula in A-2.1. This formula, applying generally to the calculated load to which superstructures and deckhouses may be exposed when protecting openings according to Regulation 18 of LL 1966/IMO is taken as a basis for the positioning of round windows. IS 12693 : 1989 B-l.3 From the graphs, the minimum height from the summer load line, S, to the sill of the round window can be derived. B-l.4 The curves given in the graphs are based on the lowest pressure which a particular type of round window can withstand. These values are given in Table 6. Table 6 Maximum Allowable Pressure, P
Type of Round Window Maximum Allowable Pressure

B-2.4 A line shall be drawn through the plotted ordinates. This line will be the lowest possible position of the sill of round windows of the particular type when situated in ships' sides or in sides of superstructure or deckhouse; however, the position is subject to the limitations given in 2.3.1 and 2.3.2. B-2.5 For round windows in fronts, the chain dotted lines in Graphs 1, 2 and 3 give the additional height which should be added to the applicable curve referred to in B-2.4. The resulting height then becomes the lowest possible position of the sill of round windows of the particular type when situated in the fronts of superstructure or deckhouses. B-2.6 For round windows of light type, used in aft ends of larger ships, Graph 4 gives the actual ordinates. The procedure to be followed is the same as given in B-2.2 to B-2.4.
NOTES 1 The particular limitations shall be observed. indicated in 2.3 and 3.2

P
kPa Heavy Medium Light 240 120 60

B-l.5 Graph 1 applies to round windows of heavy type. Graph 2 applies to round windows of medium type. Graphs 3 and 4 apply to round windows of light type. B-2 Directions for Using the Graphs B-2.1 A scale drawing ( general arrangement plan, profile drawing or capacity plan or similar showing the summer load line ) shall be used. B-2.2 The longitudinal position of the ordinates I to V shall be indicated on the plan ( see Fig. 1 ). B-2.3 The ordinate value, that is the height above the summer load line, S, or summer timber load line shall then be plotted for the type of round window being considered ( these values are obtained from either Graphs 1, 2 or 3 ).

2 The most unfavourable block coefficient ( Cb-0.6) has been chosen for all ships' lengths. Particularly, for the extreme ordinate I and to some extent also for ordinate V, the difference between the lowest and the highest values of the height above the summer load line is about 3 m and I m, respectively for a variation of Cb from 0.6 to 0% 3 Reduction of design pressure due to distance of round windows from the ship's side and due to height above deck level, in the case of round windows in fronts, is not taken into account. 4 The calculated values for the height above the summer load line, S, for the ordinates IT and V and also II1 and IV differ only by about 0.5 to 1.0 m. The pairs of ordinates are, therefore, combined in respective curves in each graph.
